cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For AX-17 in Germany, renal dose modifications are as follows:

*   **Normal renal category:** eGFR >=90, Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Monitoring Routine [E2].
*   **Mild renal category:** eGFR 60-89, Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Monitoring Routine [E2].
*   **Moderate renal category:** eGFR 30-59, Starting dose 25 mg OD, Maximum 50 mg/day, Monitoring Recheck 2-4 weeks [E2]. The approved German renal starting dose for moderate renal impairment is 25 mg once daily [E1, E3].
*   **Severe renal category:** eGFR 15-29, Specialist review, Maximum 25 mg/day, Monitoring Enhanced [E2].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
The HelixNova Safety Bulletin SB-AX17-2026-09 requires baseline hepatic laboratory values with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. It also specifies actions based on hepatic laboratory values: if ALT/AST is >3x ULN, Medical review is required; if Bilirubin is >2x ULN, Urgent review is required; and for a Mild isolated change (Below trigger), a Repeat test is required [E2]. The bulletin does not change the approved German renal starting dose of 25 mg once daily for moderate renal impairment [E1].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In study HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 included nausea (12.7%), headache (14.0%), fatigue (15.3%), dizziness (16.6%), rash (17.8%), and transaminase elevation (19.1%) [E1, E3]. For the control group in HN-204, these events were nausea (6.0%), headache (6.6%), fatigue (7.2%), dizziness (7.8%), rash (8.4%), and transaminase elevation (9.0%) [E1, E3]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-204 [E1].

In study HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 included nausea (11.8%), headache (13.0%), fatigue (14.2%), dizziness (15.4%), rash (16.6%), and transaminase elevation (17.7%) [E2, E3]. For the control group in HN-311, these events were nausea (6.0%), headache (6.6%), fatigue (7.2%), dizziness (7.8%), rash (8.4%), and transaminase elevation (9.0%) [E2, E3]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-311 [E2].

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the treatment percentages for AX-17 were lower in HN-311 for all listed adverse events: nausea (-0.9 points), headache (-1.0 points), fatigue (-1.1 points), dizziness (-1.2 points), rash (-1.2 points), and transaminase elevation (-1.4 points) [E4]. All control group percentages were identical between the two studies [E4].

In both HN-204 and HN-311, the highest treatment percentage for AX-17 was transaminase elevation, at 19.1% in HN-204 and 17.7% in HN-311 [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E3] v_adverse_events (registry database, verified read-only query) · rows for HN-204, HN-311
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

Descriptive comparison across separate studies, not a head-to-head result.
